topics.text: Physical overlap shows how much the two balls overlap along the collision line. One hundred percent represents a full-ball hit. Smaller percentages indicate a thinner hit.
topics.summary: Physical overlap shows how much the two balls overlap along the collision line.

topics.title: Travel to contact
topics.text: Cue-ball travel to contact shows the distance the cue ball travels before its predicted contact. The display expresses that distance in ball diameters, so you can compare short and long approaches.
topics.summary: Cue-ball travel to contact shows the distance the cue ball travels before its predicted contact.

topics.title: First predicted event
topics.text: First predicted event names the first major interaction the trainer shows, such as the cue ball contacting an object ball. It is a useful check that the route begins the way you planned.
topics.summary: First predicted event names the first major interaction the trainer shows, such as the cue ball contacting an object ball.

topics.title: Cue & Flight
topics.text: Cue and Flight describes the cue-tip contact and any predicted deviation or airborne behavior. This group becomes especially useful when experimenting with English, elevated cues, jumps, or mass-ay.
topics.summary: Cue and Flight describes the cue-tip contact and any predicted deviation or airborne behavior.

topics.title: Tip location
topics.text: Tip location describes where the cue tip is set to strike the cue ball. Compare this reading with your follow, draw, and left-right settings before executing the shot.
topics.summary: Tip location describes where the cue tip is set to strike the cue ball.

topics.title: Predicted squirt
topics.text: Predicted cue-ball squirt shows the initial sideways deflection associated with off-center cue contact. Compare the value as you change left or right English, and watch how the aiming path responds.
topics.summary: Predicted cue-ball squirt shows the initial sideways deflection associated with off-center cue contact.

topics.title: Jump and clearance
topics.text: Jump and flight, obstacle clearance, and jump guide provide readings for elevated shots when applicable. Use them together to check whether the cue ball will rise, clear a blocking ball, and return to the cloth. A dash means the panel is not showing a result for that item in the current setup.
topics.summary: Jump and flight, obstacle clearance, and jump guide provide readings for elevated shots when applicable.

topics.title: Curve and massé
topics.text: Curve and mass-ay describes predicted cue-ball curvature when your settings produce that type of shot. Compare the reading with the path drawn on the table as you adjust elevation, spin, and speed.
topics.summary: Curve and mass-ay describes predicted cue-ball curvature when your settings produce that type of shot.

topics.title: Power & Pocket
topics.text: Power and Pocket helps connect shot speed with ball travel. It includes a power feel reference, pocket speed, and speed readings for the cue ball and object ball.
topics.summary: Power and Pocket helps connect shot speed with ball travel.

topics.title: Power feel and pocket speed
topics.text: Power feel and pocket speed provide references for how strongly the shot is set and how the object ball will approach the pocket. Use the diamond and lag references to compare shot strength and pocket speed.
topics.summary: Power feel and pocket speed provide references for how strongly the shot is set and how the object ball will approach the pocket.

topics.title: Ball speeds
topics.text: The cue-ball-to-object-ball speed row displays speed readings associated with the approach and collision, while the object-ball-to-pocket row shows the ball speed toward the pocket. Values shown in meters per second help you compare ball speeds. Interpret them alongside friction, cut angle, and the resulting ball path.
topics.summary: The cue-ball-to-object-ball speed row displays speed readings associated with the approach and collision, while the object-ball-to-pocket row shows the ball speed toward the pocket.

topics.title: Live adjustment
topics.text: Set up a straight shot and open Live Stats. Notice the cut angle and physical overlap. Move the aim slightly to create a thinner contact, then watch both readings change. Return to a full-ball hit and compare the paths before selecting Execute Shot.
topics.summary: Set up a straight shot and open Live Stats.

topics.title: Speed and spin
topics.text: Set up a repeatable shot and open Live Stats. First adjust shot speed and compare the power and ball-speed predictions. Then restore the starting setup, change left or right English, and examine predicted squirt. Change only one setting at a time so the differences are easier to understand.
topics.summary: Set up a repeatable shot and open Live Stats.

topics.title: Power meters and Live Stats
topics.text: The C and P power meters beside the cue-ball diagram give you a quick visual check. For more detail, open Live Stats and compare the power and pocket readings as you change shot speed, aim, or spin.
topics.summary: The C and P power meters beside the cue-ball diagram give you a quick visual check.

topics.title: Follow / Draw
topics.text:
Follow gives the cue ball forward rotation. On a suitable shot, this can carry the cue ball forward after contact. Try changing the amount of follow while keeping the starting arrangement the same.

Draw gives the cue ball backspin. When enough backspin remains at contact, the cue ball can travel backward after striking the object ball. Compare different amounts of draw and shot speed.
topics.summary: Compare forward rotation and backspin.

topics.title: Impact cue ball / overlap
topics.text:
The ghost ball shows the cue-ball position needed at contact to send an object ball toward the chosen pocket. Use it as an aiming reference, then adjust the shot and examine the result.

Ball overlap describes how much of the object ball the cue ball covers along the aiming line. A fuller hit has more overlap, while a thinner cut has less. Use overlap as another way to understand the contact angle.
topics.summary: Inspect the impact cue ball and physical overlap.
